statements.text:
/-- An explicitly bilinear, nonsymmetric form with a nonzero left radical. -/
def nonsymmetricForm (v w : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ := (v.1 - v.2) * (w.1 + w.2)

theorem nonsymmetricForm_bilinear (u v w : ℝ × ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
    nonsymmetricForm (u + v) w = nonsymmetricForm u w + nonsymmetricForm v w ∧
    nonsymmetricForm u (v + w) = nonsymmetricForm u v + nonsymmetricForm u w ∧
    nonsymmetricForm (a • v) w = a * nonsymmetricForm v w ∧
    nonsymmetricForm v (a • w) = a * nonsymmetricForm v w := by

theorem complementary_axes :
    (∀ z : ℝ × ℝ, z = (0, z.2) + (z.1, 0)) ∧
    (∀ a b : ℝ, (0, a) = (b, 0) → a = 0 ∧ b = 0) := by

theorem nonsymmetric_signed_axes_singular :
    (∀ t : ℝ, t ≠ 0 → nonsymmetricForm (0, t) (0, t) < 0) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, t ≠ 0 → 0 < nonsymmetricForm (t, 0) (t, 0)) ∧
    ((1, 1) : ℝ × ℝ) ≠ 0 ∧
    (∀ w : ℝ × ℝ, nonsymmetricForm (1, 1) w = 0) ∧
    nonsymmetricForm (1, 0) (0, 1) = 1 ∧
    nonsymmetricForm (0, 1) (1, 0) = -1 := by

/-- Literal criticality alone does not imply differentiability: fderiv defaults
to zero at a nondifferentiable point. This example is not claimed periodic. -/
theorem nonsmooth_literal_critical :
    (¬ DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun x : E 1 => ‖x‖) 0) ∧
    IsCriticalPoint 1 (fun x : E 1 => ‖x‖) 0 := by

/-- A half-open representative domain cannot supply compactness by itself. -/
theorem half_open_not_compact :
    ¬ IsCompact (Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1) := by
theorem closed_interval_compact : IsCompact (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) := isCompact_Icc

items.title: C294 conditional death-height attainment on the period-lattice torus quotient. Given local path connectivity of the closed death superlevel, a path from M to a strictly older critical point stays at or above superlevelBar_deathHeight g M and attains it (TorusCriticalAttainment.quotient_death_attainment, euclidean_death_attainment).

statements.text:
theorem quotient_death_attainment (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (g : E d → ℝ) (hsmooth : IsSmooth d g) (hperiodic : IsLPeriodic d L g)
    (hmorse : IsMorseDistinct d L g) (M : E d)
    (hnonessential : ¬ superlevelBar_isEssential g M)
    (hclosedLPC : LocallyPathConnectedSpace
      {q : torus_quotient d L hL //
        superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic q}) :
    ∃ Q ∈ quotientCriticalSet d L hL g,
      g M < descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic Q ∧
      ∃ γ : Path (torus_proj d L hL M) Q,
        (∀ t : unitInterval,
          superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic (γ t)) ∧
        ∃ t : unitInterval,
          descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic (γ t) = superlevelBar_deathHeight g M := by

theorem euclidean_death_attainment (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (g : E d → ℝ) (hsmooth : IsSmooth d g) (hperiodic : IsLPeriodic d L g)
    (hmorse : IsMorseDistinct d L g) (M : E d)
    (hnonessential : ¬ superlevelBar_isEssential g M)
    (hclosedLPC : LocallyPathConnectedSpace
      {q : torus_quotient d L hL //
        superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic q}) :
    ∃ y : E d, IsCriticalPoint d g y ∧ g M < g y ∧
      ∃ Γ : Path M y,
        (∀ t : unitInterval, superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ g (Γ t)) ∧
        ∃ t : unitInterval, g (Γ t) = superlevelBar_deathHeight g M := by

statements.text: A deterministic update is constant on each cell of \(A_t\). If one available cell intersects two required cells of \(R_t\), no update can refine \(R_t\). That cell is an obstruction witness.

For a deterministic update \(M_t=f(A_t)\),

\[
H(R_t|M_t)\geq H(R_t|A_t).
\]

For task loss \(L\),

\[
\rho_L(R|M_t)\geq \rho_L(R|A_t).
\]

Every decision rule measurable with respect to \(M_t\) is also measurable with respect to \(A_t\). The information-loss defect is

\[
D_L(M_t;A_t)=\rho_L(R|M_t)-\rho_L(R|A_t)\geq0.
\]

For static exact support of required partitions \(P_1,\ldots,P_T\), memory must refine

\[
P_*=\bigvee_{t=1}^{T}P_t.
\]

For multiple tasks, minimize a vector of risks rather than assuming one scalar optimum. Memories can form MI–risk or multitask Pareto frontiers. Task mutual information and Bayes risk genuinely diverge in the included three-state observation model.

The deterministic specialized memories have minimax option risk \(0.25\). A 50/50 randomized mixture has distribution-level minimax risk \(0.125\). A realization-level adversary still obtains \(0.25\). Under expected loss, the robust memory is not automatically optimal; it becomes preferable only under specified hard constraints or noise regimes.

For independent binary symmetric channels with rates \(\alpha\) on \(x\) and \(\beta\) on \(z\), the specialized option risks are

\[
A_0=0.25\alpha+0.5(1-\alpha)\beta,
\qquad
A_1=0.25-0.25\alpha+0.5\alpha\beta.
\]

The full-observation floor is \((\alpha,\beta/2,\beta/2)\). A balanced specialized mixture has distribution-level minimax risk

\[
U_{\mathrm{dist}}=0.125+0.25\beta.
\]

A realization-level adversary obtains

\[
U_{\mathrm{real}}=0.25-0.25\alpha+0.5\alpha\beta.
\]

The exact gap is

\[
U_{\mathrm{real}}-U_{\mathrm{dist}}
=0.125(1-2\alpha)(1-2\beta).
\]

It vanishes when either channel is pure noise. Under balanced option uncertainty, the robust memory is expected-loss preferable to the balanced specialized mixture when \(2\alpha-\beta>1/2\).

Let \(\kappa=P(\text{both observations flip})\), with independence at \(\kappa=\alpha\beta\). Correlation changes posterior cell weights and can switch optimal decisions. The visibility gap is then piecewise rather than universally factorized.

For \(\alpha=0.2,\beta=0.3\), the independent formula predicts gap \(0.03\). The exact correlated model gives gap \(0\) at \(\kappa=0\), \(0.03\) at \(\kappa=0.06\), and \(0.05\) at \(\kappa=0.10\) and \(0.20\). The factorization is therefore independence-specific.
